note: Set A and Set B are nearly identical: all 24 of B's claims appear in A, in the same wording, so they share the same strengths (root/tip prebend, tip twist, pitch-axis endpoints, thickness trend) and the same defects (repeated claims for the same fact, several values that conflict with each other or with the plotted curves, and quotes that are only axis labels). A adds one further claim, chord = 5.7 m at r/R = 0.25, which is consistent with the chord plot near its maximum (~5.7–5.8 m), so A captures an extra correct fact that B omits. Because the added claim is supported and nothing wrong is added, A is marginally better; the shared misreadings and duplicates weigh equally on both.
remarks: Both sets contain internally conflicting claims for the same condition: twist at r/R=0 given as 14, 15 and 15.5 deg (curve starts near 15.5–16), relative thickness at r/R=0 given as 95 and 100 % (curve starts at 100), and chord at r/R=1.0 given as both 1.5 m and 0.5 m (the curve is ~1.5 m just before the tip and drops to ~0.5 m at the very end). Relative thickness 22 % at r/R=0.7 is quoted against the tick label '20' and reads high on the curve (~23–25 %), and chord 5.2 m at r/R=0.2 is below the plotted maximum (~5.8 m). Nearly all quotes are axis or subplot labels and do not substantiate the numeric values, which are only readable from the plotted curves; exact values at intermediate stations are approximate. Both sets also leave out the chord maximum near r/R≈0.2 and the twist minimum near r/R≈0.85 as explicit facts.
